title: Sound: pitch and amplitude
target: Use a longitudinal-wave model to distinguish pitch and sound level.
criteria: Separate particle motion from sound propagation.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: In a sound wave in air, what is a compression?
options: A permanent pile of air at the speaker.
A region with no air molecules.
A region of higher pressure and density than equilibrium.
A sideways motion of all air across the room.
cpa.guide: Longitudinal sound produces alternating pressure/density increases and decreases.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Which description represents a rarefaction in an air sound wave?
options: A vacuum that must persist forever.
A region where sound becomes electromagnetic.
A pressure maximum.
A local pressure and density decrease relative to equilibrium.
cpa.guide: Rarefaction is a lower-pressure portion of the oscillating medium.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Tones A and B have equal amplitudes. Frequencies are 350 Hz and 700 Hz. Which has higher pitch?
options: Both must have the same pitch because amplitude is equal.
A.
B.
Neither has pitch because frequency is positive.
cpa.guide: Pitch is primarily associated with frequency; B has the higher frequency.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A speaker doubles displacement amplitude while keeping its driving frequency fixed. Which statement is best?
options: Sound speed must double in the same air.
Sound intensity can increase while pitch remains approximately unchanged.
Pitch must double.
Frequency must halve.
cpa.guide: Amplitude mainly affects intensity; pitch depends mainly on frequency.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Sound travels east through air. In the simple longitudinal model, how do nearby air particles move?
options: Back and forth approximately east-west around their equilibrium positions.
Only north-south.
Continuously east all the way to the listener.
They remain perfectly still while pressure changes.
cpa.guide: Particle motion is parallel to propagation but oscillatory, not bulk transport from speaker to listener.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A distant clap is heard before any breeze from the source arrives. What distinction explains this?
options: Sound in air requires no medium.
Sound is the same as bulk wind speed.
Air particles must move at light speed.
A pressure disturbance propagates; the original source air need not travel to the listener.
cpa.guide: Signal propagation differs from the bulk transport of the source material.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
